description: A flock of Hyderabad hackers building a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer, so anyone can see and map the stars. And... We’re recruiting! Coders, designers, storytellers, space nerds, physics nerds, and anyone who can explain orbits to a 10-year-old effectively are welcome. No astronaut credentials required. Bring curiosity, snacks, and a tolerance for pigeon puns. Join us and help the next generation reach for the stars (and not get stuck in the airlock).
summary:
SphereX is an interactive astronomical exploration and scientific analysis platform developed to transform NASA’s SPHEREx data into accessible, meaningful scientific insights.

Addressing the Planet X and SPHEREx challenge, our platform enables users to explore celestial objects through an interactive sky map, visualize changes over time, and investigate astronomical phenomena across infrared wavelengths. SphereX integrates real astronomical observations, eight scientific analysis lenses, interactive 3D spectral cube visualizations, and an experimental machine learning pipeline designed to identify celestial motion, objects, and potential anomalies.

By combining astronomical data processing, artificial intelligence, and intuitive visualization within a unified platform, SphereX reduces the technical barriers associated with analysing complex astronomical datasets.

Our objective is to democratize astronomical research, empowering researchers, students, and citizen scientists to investigate celestial phenomena, identify overlooked patterns, and contribute to the search for undiscovered objects within our universe. SphereX transforms astronomical observation from a passive experience into an opportunity for active scientific discovery.
details:
The platform combines an interactive celestial map, time-series visualizations, eight scientific analysis lenses, and interactive 3D spectral cube visualization, enabling users to explore the universe across spatial, temporal, and spectral dimensions. It integrates real astronomical observations from the IRSA archive with locally stored datasets to support reliable data accessibility.

SphereX also incorporates experimental machine learning for detecting celestial objects, identifying motion, and highlighting potential astronomical anomalies, reducing the complexity of manually interpreting large astronomical datasets.

By bridging the gap between raw astronomical data and meaningful scientific insights, SphereX aims to transform passive observation into active scientific exploration, democratizing astronomical research and creating opportunities for new discoveries.
